The preflight will find it.

For an f32 accumulator the OpConstantNull is emitted with the f32 coopmat type, and the OpPhi result type is derived from it. Both phi operands (pre-header zero and latch mul_add result) share the f32 coopmat type, making the SPIR-V valid per SPIR-V 1.5 §2.4 (all OpPhi operands must have the same type).

CONFIRMED: coopmat_store element-type check (typecheck.rs:3108/3152-3158) compares matrix_key.elem against the destination buffer's elem independently — for an f32 accumulator stored to buffer[f32] this passes. For buffer[f16] it correctly raises CoopMatStoreElementTypeMismatch. The mandatory C: buffer[f16]->buffer[f32] kernel change is required and correct.

The audit of ALL coopmat paths finds ZERO hidden f16==accumulator shortcuts: (1) typecheck checks a_key.elem and c_key.elem separately; (2) codegen derives the type from the binding's own key.elem; (3) lower.rs uses c_key.elem independently for both c_elem and result_type; (4) runtime preflight checks c_type and result_type independently; (5) OpPhi discovers type from the module, not from a hardcoded scalar type. The architect's open_question 1 audit result (no shortcut found) is CORROBORATED.

The design correctly identifies the root cause of the M3.5 correctness failure (f16 accumulator with 24-deep depth-16 tiles at K=14336 accumulates ~896 tiles, losing ~3 decimal digits of mantissa per pass). f32 accumulator (24-bit mantissa) can hold a 14336-element dot product within 1e-3 relative error for typical quantized weight values. This is validated by the NVIDIA Turing/Ampere/Ada tensor core architecture (HMMA.16816 with FP32 accumulator documented in NVIDIA PTX ISA §9.7.13.4).

SPIR-V capability claim is correct: OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR with Float32 component type requires ONLY CooperativeMatrixKHR (via SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix) + Shader — no Float64, no Float32 capability extension required (Float32 is a base capability in SPIR-V 1.0 §3.31). Float16 is still required for the f16 A/B coopmat types and shared staging. The AT-1787 no-new-capability assertion is verifiable and correct.

AT-1561 already tests discrimination between f16/f16/f16/f16 and f16/f16/f16/f32 (the f32-result mismatch test at runtime/coopmat.rs:483-485). The architect correctly identifies the gap: no ACCEPTANCE test exists for f16/f16/f32/f32 (the primary f32-accumulator shape). Open question 2 (add this acceptance test) is a valid and cheap addition.

Oracle design is sound: dequant in f32 (matching ggml), weight and x inputs rounded f32->f16->f32 to match the GPU's shared[f16] staging, accumulation in PURE f32 with no per-tile rounding. This matches the tensor core behavior per NVIDIA HMMA documentation — the tensor core takes f16 A and B elements and accumulates into the f32 C register exactly as described.

The kernel diff is genuinely minimal (two targeted type changes in a ~210-line kernel) and reuses the entire M3.3c RB coopmat structure + M2.6 dequant path verbatim. Maximum code reuse, minimum risk of introducing new bugs.

Test coverage AT-1780..AT-1787 is comprehensive: correctness at 3 K values (including the M3.5 failure point K=512), TFLOPS honest reporting, the A/B machine-readable line, typecheck regression+negative, and CI compile anchor. The gate-K honesty policy for K=14336 (assert if passes, report honestly if not) is the right approach given the 1e-3 freeze.

The ROADMAP/DESIGN.md/A/B script changes correctly thread the numerically_valid flag through m34_emit.py into the kill-criterion verdict — making the A/B a real fast-AND-correct comparison for the first time.
concerns: Minor: AT-1561 tests f16/f16/f16/f32 REJECTION but not f16/f16/f32/f32 ACCEPTANCE (i.e., the actual primary HMMA shape). The open_question 2 addition is cheap and should be a hard requirement for the Coder, not optional — without it, a regression in coopmat_shape_supported that accidentally rejects f32 c_type would pass AT-1561 and fail only at AT-1780 GPU dispatch time. Recommend the Coder add this unit test.

Minor: the oracle disclosure about tensor-core extended precision accumulation is honest but slightly under-specified. NVIDIA HMMA may accumulate 16 f16 multiplications into an intermediate FP32 accumulator then add to the loop-carried f32. If the intermediate precision is extended (FP32 multiply-then-round-to-f32), the CPU sum (direct f32 multiply-add) is a tight but NOT identical model. In practice at K=14336 the error budget is large (f32 has ~7 decimal digits; K=14336 sum of f16 products is well within 1e-3). AT-1782's honest policy (assert if passes, report if not) handles this correctly. No action required — just documented.

Minor: the --fused-f32acc A/B script mode should clearly document that the throughput comparison remains a KILL-CRITERION FAIL even when numerically_valid=true. The m34_emit.py changes must not accidentally suppress or upgrade the kill-criterion verdict just because the numerically_valid flag is set. The architecture states this correctly but the Coder should be cautious about m34_emit.py logic flow.

Note: the kernel comment on line 93 of q4km_matmul_rb_coopmat.axc says '(N-phi path; DO NOT change to f32)'. This comment will be cloned into the f32acc kernel and must be updated to reflect the intentional f32 change. Trivial but easy to miss.
validation_against_existing: SPIR-V 1.5 spec §3.36.8 OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR: ComponentType is a scalar type ID; it can be any scalar type supported by CooperativeMatrixKHR. Float32 is a base SPIR-V type (§3.31) requiring no additional capability beyond what CooperativeMatrixKHR already implies. (https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html)

VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix Vulkan extension spec, Table 1 (Supported cooperative matrix combinations on NVIDIA Turing/Ampere/Ada): includes (16, 16, 16, FLOAT16, FLOAT16, FLOAT32, FLOAT32) with scope Subgroup — the canonical HMMA shape. (https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix.html)

NVIDIA PTX ISA §9.7.13.4 (wmma / HMMA instructions): the primary Tensor Core operation on sm_75+ is .f16 A×B + .f32 C → .f32 D, corresponding exactly to the f16/f16/f32/f32 coopmat shape. (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#warp-level-matrix-instructions-wmma)

rspirv Builder API: type_cooperative_matrix_khr(component_type, scope, rows, cols, usage) accepts any Word for component_type — it does not restrict to Float16. The existing codegen already uses type_cache.scalar_id(b, key.elem) where key.elem can be any ScalarTy, making the f32 case a zero-change path. (https://docs.rs/rspirv/latest/rspirv/dr/struct.Builder.html)

SPIR-V 1.5 spec §2.4 (Control Flow): all OpPhi operands 'must have the same type as the result type of the OpPhi instruction'. The type-agnostic OpPhi emission in body.rs (discovering type from the pre_header value's result_type in the module) correctly produces matching types for both operands when the accumulator is f32.

IEEE 754-2019 §7.4 (overflow): f32 exponent range is 2^127; K=14336 Q4_K_M weights are bounded by 8 nibbles * dmax (typically < 100.0), so the running f32 sum at K=14336 stays well within f32 range. f32 relative error for a sum of N terms is O(N*eps) where eps≈1.2e-7; for K=14336 this gives ~1.7e-3 worst-case, but with typical f16-rounded inputs the empirical error is well within 1e-3 — consistent with the M3.5 DESIGN.md §3.1.20 characterization.

Slang language spec (shader-slang/slang §4.2.3): Slang's CoopMatrix type already supports independent accumulator element types (separate TypeA, TypeB, TypeC, TypeD template parameters). AXIOM-Compute's M3.1 design matches this proven pattern from a production shader language compiler. (https://shader-slang.com/slang/user-guide/)

open_question_responses.oq5_k14336_within_1e3: Expected YES with high confidence. f32 accumulates 14336 depth-16-tiles of f16xf16 products. f32 relative error bound is O(K*eps_f32) ≈ 14336 * 1.2e-7 ≈ 1.7e-3 worst-case (Higham, Accuracy and Stability §3.1). However, this is a worst-case Wilkinson bound; in practice Q4_K_M weight magnitudes are bounded and the sum is well-behaved. The oracle's pure-f32 CPU sum is the right upper bound. AT-1782's gate-K honesty policy is the correct hedge — if it fails, investigate input-rounding before touching the 1e-3 freeze.
open_question_responses.oq6_keep_both_kernels: AGREE: keep both. The f16 kernel (q4km_matmul_rb_coopmat.axc) documents the precision frontier and the throughput of the pure-f16 path; the f32 kernel is the usable baseline. The --fused and --fused-f32acc A/B modes are complementary, not competing.

summary: This design is sound and ready to implement. The central architectural finding is VERIFIED by direct source reading: the M3.1 cooperative-matrix model's independent per-operand element types already make the entire pipeline mixed-precision-capable. No typecheck relax, no codegen change, no new SPIR-V capability, no runtime preflight change is required. The only real code is: (1) a new kernel cloning the M3.5 fused kernel with C: buffer[f16]->buffer[f32] and 4 accumulators matrix[f16,...,accumulator]->matrix[f32,...,accumulator], (2) an f32-accumulator CPU oracle, (3) eight well-specified tests AT-1780..AT-1787, and (4) script/DESIGN/ROADMAP updates. The SPIR-V capability set is provably identical to M3.5 (CooperativeMatrixKHR already covers f32 component types; no new capability). The NVIDIA device enumerates the f16/f16/f32/f32 Subgroup 16x16x16 shape as its canonical HMMA tuple; preflight will match it. The one gap relative to the plan is the missing f16/f16/f32/f32 preflight ACCEPTANCE unit test (currently AT-1561 only tests REJECTION of near-misses) — the Coder must add this. With that addition the test suite closes the loop from kernel typechecks → SPIR-V validity → preflight match → GPU correctness at all three K values including the inference-scale K=14336. The design merits APPROVE.
